wordsPreamble:
- Lithuanian is one of the oldest living Indo-European languages, keeping sounds and endings that most relatives lost long ago.
- Most young people in Vilnius speak good English. Many older people speak Russian or Polish too.
- Š is “sh,” ž is “zh,” č is “ch,” and y is a long “ee.”
- Vilnius has been Lithuanian, Polish (as Wilno), and Jewish (as Vilna, in Yiddish). All three names are part of its story.
